$comment: Single source of truth for which crafts a build offers AND what language it speaks. `registry` maps a BUNDLED craft (built from crafts/<id>/ in this repo, served at /<id>/index.html) to its panel label; a label may be a string or a per-locale object {en, zh-CN}. Every other craft lives in the craft registry (https://github.com/logisky/crafts), published at `craftRegistry`; the app downloads and installs those at RUNTIME. `distributions` define named build targets; pick one at build time with the CRAFT_DIST env var (default: 'default'). A distribution's `crafts` are the bundled crafts it ships; its `install` are registry craft ids the app installs automatically the first time it starts online (each at most once: one the user uninstalls stays uninstalled); `defaultCraft` may name either kind. `devInstall` is added to `install` by the dev server only. A distribution's `locale` becomes the app's DEFAULT language (injected as __APP_LOCALE__; a language the user picks explicitly outranks it). Consumed by Vite (craft lists, registry URL + locale, via `define` in vite.config.ts), publish-crafts.sh (what lands in dist/, via scripts/craft-dist.mjs) and the desktop CI (product name/id/title, via `craft-dist.mjs tauri`). A registry entry marked `devOnly` is offered ONLY by the dev server: it stays in `registry` (so dist/ pruning still removes it) but is filtered out of every distribution's craft list, so it is never published or bundled.

en.$comment: English desktop release. Excludes the Chinese-only game crafts.

zh.$comment: Chinese desktop release. ASCII product name, so every Windows bundler (incl. MSI) works.
